By the way, what's the point of setting `-trimpath` when running `go test`?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> By the way, what's the point of setting -trimpath when running go test?

We are setting a global `GOFLAGS` for the build which contains `-trimpath`.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Reopening it as I can reproduce it on an Ubuntu 24.04 image with go 1.22.2.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @participant2 Hi, any idea why this test doesn't work on some systems?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Reopening it as I can reproduce it on an Ubuntu 24.04 image with go 1.22.2.

Setting GOROOT fixed the issue:

```sh
GOROOT=$(go env GOROOT) go test -trimpath ./...
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Right, but `GOROOT` is a new requirement so this is either something missing in the test (API breakage?) or something amiss with the library being used (regression?)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I've no idea to be honest. The test code was written by @participant2 and I'm not fully familiar with the libraries used in it. Considering that it works without `GOROOT` on macOS, maybe it's a bug in the Go distribution or the Linux package? 

Anyway, this `GOROOT` requirement doesn't apply to `build` command, and it actually makes more sense to not use `-trimpath` in `test` context (see https://github.com/golang/vscode-go/issues/2737), I think it's fine.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Thank you for flaggifng this and I'll take a look at fixing this with `-trimpath` when I have some cycles but that might be a few days. Basically, the goal of this test is to ensure that `os.Exit` is not called, I could look at how [golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis](https://<redacted-host>/golang.org/x/tools@v0.20.0/go/analysis) works since it performs similar analysis and see if it handles `-trimpath` being set.

That said, I'm not sure `-trimpath` provides much benefit when running tests - IIRC it's mostly for distributing builds.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Thank you for flaggifng this and I'll take a look at fixing this with -trimpath when I have some cycles but that might be a few days. 

Thanks for looking at it. I tried looking at the code initially but didn't get very far.

> That said, I'm not sure -trimpath provides much benefit when running tests - IIRC it's mostly for distributing builds.

I don't disagree on this, but build systems in distros sets a global `GOFLAGS` variable and having to replace out `-trimpath` because the test fails when it's set is not optimal.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> build systems in distros sets a global `GOFLAGS` variable and having to replace out `-trimpath`

How about setting `GOROOT` as well instead of removing `-trimpath`? Seems like an easier and safer approach.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: `GOROOT=$(go env GOROOT)` is inherently redundant, I'm curious why this has regressed.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
A quick research.

`build.ImportDir` refers to `runtime.GOROOT()`,

* https://github.com/golang/go/blob/16ce8b3925deaeb72541ee96b6ee23a08fc21dea/src/go/build/build.go#L310-L317

and this is the definition of `runtime.GOROOT()`:

* https://github.com/golang/go/blob/16ce8b3925deaeb72541ee96b6ee23a08fc21dea/src/runtime/extern.go#L331-L342
* https://github.com/golang/go/blob/16ce8b3925deaeb72541ee96b6ee23a08fc21dea/src/runtime/extern.go#L257-L262

But `go env` seems to do more work to than just referring to it to locate the real `GOROOT`.

* https://github.com/golang/go/blob/16ce8b3925deaeb72541ee96b6ee23a08fc21dea/src/cmd/go/internal/cfg/cfg.go#L472

So that I think explains why the test requires `GOROOT`. So until they clear up the differences, `GOROOT=$(go env GOROOT)` is the only option. It may seem redundant, but it isn't for now, and it's safe and future-proof.
